note: Frozen explanatory structural model for the DFlow route-stable bracket experiment. This file is authored, not derived: it states assumed structure, evidence class and claim ceiling. It deliberately carries no empirical counts — those live in route_stable_batch_evidence.json and eligible_byte_evidence.json, so the two cannot drift apart. A repository test enforces that.
not_a_claim: This is not a fitted model and contains no probabilities or effect sizes.
The route-stable contrast is not a Pearl controlled direct effect: route was selected on, never intervened on.
No arrow here asserts that slippage caused any observed reroute.

caused.label: Exact response relation
caused.description: A named response field follows a stated integer relation to the parameter that was set, in every capture.

together.label: Observed together
together.description: Both moved in the same captures, but the design cannot attribute one to the other.

candidate.label: Candidate byte match
candidate.description: A value appears as a literal at a recurring position under the tested encoding family. Not semantic decoding.

not_observed.label: Not identified under this search
not_observed.description: Not recovered under the encoding family tested, or outside the observation boundary entirely.

intervention_supported.label: Intervention-supported
intervention_supported.description: A parameter was set by the experimenter and the downstream response was observed to follow an exact stated relation within this experiment.

observed_covariation.label: Observed covariation
observed_covariation.description: Both endpoints were observed to move together across captures. Direction is assumed from the structure, not demonstrated.

candidate.label: Candidate encoding
candidate.description: A byte-equality match that recurs across eligible brackets. Not a decoded protocol field.

hypothesized.label: Hypothesized
hypothesized.description: Structural assumption used to reason about the design. Not identified by this experiment.

unobserved.label: Outside observation boundary
unobserved.description: Nothing was signed or submitted, so this relation produced no observation at all.

nodes.label: S
nodes.name: slippageBps
nodes.definition: Requested slippage tolerance, in basis points, sent on the /order request. This is the only quantity set by the experimenter.
nodes.evidence: Set directly by the bracket runner. Anchors 50 bps; treatments 10 and 100 bps.
nodes.ceiling: Intervened on directly. No inference required.

nodes.label: U
nodes.name: market state
nodes.definition: Contemporaneous market and venue state at request time: inventory, quotes and liquidity across the venues the router can reach.
nodes.evidence: Never measured. Its movement is only detected indirectly, through drift between the two 50 bps anchors.
nodes.ceiling: Unmeasured. The bracket detects that it may have moved; it does not control it.

nodes.label: R
nodes.name: routePlan
nodes.definition: The route topology returned by the provider: venues, market keys, leg order and allocation. Fingerprinted before any results were inspected.
nodes.evidence: Observed on every request and hashed into a route fingerprint that was frozen before any live results were inspected.
nodes.ceiling: Observed, but selected on rather than assigned. Selecting on R is not do(R).

nodes.label: Q
nodes.name: outAmount
nodes.definition: Quoted output amount for the order, in token base units.
nodes.ceiling: Directly observed in the response body.

nodes.label: M
nodes.name: otherAmountThreshold
nodes.definition: Minimum-output threshold carried on the order. Equal to minOutAmount in every observation.
nodes.evidence: Follows an exact integer relation to the quoted amount and the requested slippage. Verified match counts are carried by the evidence extract, not by this file.
nodes.ceiling: Exact within this experiment and this execution mode. Not asserted as a universal provider rule.

nodes.label: B
nodes.name: unsigned transaction
nodes.definition: The unsigned versioned Solana transaction returned with the order: instructions, payloads, accounts and address-lookup tables.
nodes.evidence: Decoded for every request. In eligible brackets, exactly one instruction payload changed.
nodes.ceiling: Bytes are observed. Field semantics are not: no IDL or official decoder was used.

nodes.label: Y
nodes.name: settlement
nodes.definition: Realized settlement: landed transaction, delivery path and filled price.
nodes.evidence: None. Nothing was signed and nothing was submitted.
nodes.ceiling: Entirely outside the observation boundary of this experiment.

edges.label: may influence routing
edges.note: Structurally possible: the router may take the tolerance into account. This experiment does not show it. Reroutes were observed both with and without a treatment change, and market state moved at the same time.
edges.ceiling: Not identified. Do not read any reroute in this data as caused by slippage.

edges.label: market state moves routing
edges.note: The two 50 bps anchors returned different routes in several brackets with no parameter change between them, which is consistent with routing that tracks market state.
edges.ceiling: Consistent with the data; not separately identified.

edges.label: route shapes the quote
edges.note: Quoted output differs across requests that also differ in route. The two sources of variation are not separated here.

edges.label: market state moves the quote
edges.note: Quoted output drifted between the two anchors even when the route fingerprint was identical.
edges.ceiling: Consistent with the data; not separately identified.

edges.label: quote feeds the threshold
edges.note: Part of the exact integer identity M = ceil(Q * (10000 - S) / 10000), which held for all 30 observations.

edges.label: slippage sets the threshold
edges.note: The intervened parameter enters the threshold directly: setting S moves M exactly as the integer identity predicts.
edges.ceiling: Exact within this experiment and this execution mode.

edges.equation: B := f_B(R, Q, M, accounts, provider state, ...)
edges.label: route shapes construction
edges.note: When the route fingerprint changed, program sets and account topology changed with it. This is why route-unstable brackets are excluded before any byte comparison.

edges.equation: B := f_B(R, Q, M, accounts, provider state, ...)
edges.label: candidate byte match
edges.note: In the eligible brackets the quoted output value matched a literal inside one instruction payload, at a position that recurred across every request searched. Location, coverage and canonical encoding come from the byte-evidence extract.
edges.ceiling: Byte equality is not semantic decoding. This offset is not established as the protocol's outAmount field.

edges.equation: B := f_B(R, Q, M, accounts, provider state, ...)
edges.label: threshold not located
edges.note: The threshold was one of the three quantities searched for in the instruction payloads. It produced no match in any eligible bracket.
edges.ceiling: Not identified in this experiment. Absence of a byte-equality match is not proof the threshold is absent from the transaction: it may be encoded, scaled or packed differently.

edges.label: never observed
edges.note: No signature, no submission, no delivery, no fill.
edges.ceiling: Outside the observation boundary by design.

collider.explanation: Route sits downstream of both the intervened parameter and the unmeasured market state. Keeping only brackets whose route stayed stable is a selection rule applied to that shared child. Selecting on a common child can associate its two parents even when one of them was set externally.
collider.consequence: The eligible comparison is a cleaner forensic window, not a randomized mediator experiment. It should not be described as a controlled direct effect.

modes.label: Structural model
modes.summary: The assumed structure. Line style and badge show how much support each arrow actually has.

modes.label: Intervention
modes.summary: Only S was set by the experimenter. Nothing upstream of S remains: the parameter was assigned, not observed. Downstream arrows show what could propagate, not what was identified.

modes.label: Route-stable selection
modes.summary: Eligibility keeps only brackets whose route topology held still. That is a selection rule on R, a shared child of S and U. Observed route stability is a selection rule, not an intervention on route.

modes.label: Evidence
modes.summary: What this experiment actually supports: an exact quote-stage identity, one recurring candidate byte match, one quantity searched for and not found, and a settlement path with no observations at all.
